content.title: UNC Charlotte fires basketball coach days after making tournament semifinals
content.text: CHARLOTTE, N.C. (WBTV) - The Charlotte 49ers fired their men’s basketball coach, just days after the school played in the American Conference tournament semifinals.UNC Charlotte confirmed it fired head coach Aaron Fearne on Tuesday, March 17.“We have high expectations for all of our athletic programs at Charlotte, and while difficult, making a head coaching change is necessary to allow for greater success,” new 49ers athletic director Kevin White said in a statement.Fearne was Charlotte’s head coach for most of three seasons, beginning early in the 2023-2024 campaign. Prior to that, he was an assistant at Charlotte for five seasons, and coached professional basketball in Australia before that.The 49ers posted a 47-51 record over Fearne’s three seasons, and went 17-17 this year.Charlotte finished fifth in the American Conference this season and advanced to the tournament semifinals, where the 49ers lost to South Florida, 86-64. South Florida went on to win the conference championship game the next day.The university said a national search would be done to find the school’s next head coach.UNC Charlotte has not made the NCAA tournament since 2005.UNC Charlotte fired men's basketball head coach Aaron Fearne on March 17.(Matt Kelley | AP)Also Read: Major NASCAR team could expand campus further into Mecklenburg CountyCopyright 2026 WBTV.
